items.author: manucohenyashar
items.body:
We should support integration with RDF knowledge graphs, not just labeled property graphs, such as Neo4j.

RDF is required to enable semantic inference for building a rich context. 
Fun fact about the context: Most of it is never written anywhere because it is inferred. 
For example, just by examining the company's organizational chart, we can **infer** permissions, areas of expertise, geographic locations, and more. It is impossible to write down all the facts, but enough facts, along with a few inference rules (i.e., ontology), can tell us the whole story.	

RDF and OWL will enable contextua

items.author: blolt
items.body:
## Summary

Graphiti currently requires an external graph database server (Neo4j, FalkorDB, etc.) to function. This adds a barrier for lightweight, local use cases — personal assistants, local-first AI agents, CLI tools, quick prototyping, and CI/CD pipelines — where spinning up a database server is excessive overhead.

[FalkorDB Lite](https://github.com/FalkorDB/falkordblite) (`falkordblite`) is an embedded variant of FalkorDB that runs as a subprocess with file-based storage. No server, no Docker, no configuration — just a file path.

## Motivation

As Graphiti adoption grows beyond server-s
items.title: feat: Add FalkorDB Lite support for embedded, zero-config graph storage

`resolve_extracted_nodes` in `graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/node_operations.py` fetches **all existing nodes** from the graph and passes them to the LLM in a single call for entity deduplication. As the graph grows, the prompt size grows linearly (O(n)), eventually exceeding the model's `max_tokens` limit and causing the entire episode ingestion to fail.

### Observed behavior

With ~300+ episodes across multiple knowledge groups, resolution calls hit `Output length exceeded max tokens 16384` consistently:

